title: Interstate banking deregulation on credit supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID). The treatment is interstate banking deregulation occurring in period 4 for the treated group. The key assumption is parallel trends: in the absence of deregulation, treated and control states would have followed similar trajectories in their loans-to-assets ratios. This is plausible since banking regulations were similar across states prior to deregulation, and economic fundamentals driving credit demand should move similarly across states.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# Read the data
data <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s05_data.csv")

# Basic summary statistics
cat("=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
print(summary(data))

cat("\n=== TREATMENT ASSIGNMENT ===\n")
table(data$treated, data$period)

# Main DID regression with unit and time fixed effects
cat("\n=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===\n")
main_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)
print(main_model)

# Extract and display the main coefficient
did_coeff <- coef(main_model)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("\nMain DID Coefficient: %.4f\n", did_coeff))

# Robustness check 1: Pre-trend test
# Create leads and lags of treatment
data[, period_relative := period - 4]  # Period 4 is treatment
data[, treated_period := ifelse(treated == 1, period_relative, NA)]

# Create event study specification with period -1 as omitted category
data[, pre_3 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == -3)]
data[, pre_2 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == -2)]
# pre_1 omitted as reference
data[, post_0 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == 0)]
data[, post_1 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == 1)]
data[, post_2 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == 2)]
data[, post_3 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == 3)]
data[, post_4 := as.numeric(treated == 1 & period_relative == 4)]

cat("\n=== EVENT STUDY (PRE-TREND TEST) ===\n")
event_model <- feols(y ~ pre_3 + pre_2 + post_0 + post_1 + post_2 + post_3 + post_4 | 
                     unit_id + period, data = data)
print(event_model)

# Test for pre-trends
pre_coeffs <- coef(event_model)[c("pre_3", "pre_2")]
cat(sprintf("\nPre-treatment coefficients:\nPre-3: %.4f\nPre-2: %.4f\n", 
            pre_coeffs["pre_3"], pre_coeffs["pre_2"]))

# Robustness check 2: Alternative specification without unit FE
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: NO UNIT FIXED EFFECTS ===\n")
robust_model1 <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post | period, data = data)
print(robust_model1)

# Robustness check 3: Clustered standard errors at unit level
cat("\n=== MAIN MODEL WITH CLUSTERED SEs ===\n")
main_model_cluster <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                           data = data, cluster = "unit_id")
print(main_model_cluster)

# Final summary of key results
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULTS SUMMARY ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Main DID Effect: %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(main_model_cluster)["treat_x_post"],
            se(main_model_cluster)["treat_x_post"]))
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.4f\n", pvalue(main_model_cluster)["treat_x_post"]))

# Calculate average treatment effect in levels (approximate)
cat(sprintf("Approximate percentage point change in loans/assets ratio: %.2f pp\n", 
            did_coeff * 100))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient of approximately 0.10-0.20, indicating that interstate banking deregulation increased the loans-to-assets ratio by 10-20 percentage points. The economic logic is that deregulation allows banks to operate across state lines, increasing competition for deposits and lending opportunities, which should lead to expanded credit supply. Banks in deregulated states can tap into broader markets and diversify risk geographically, enabling them to increase their lending relative to assets. The magnitude should be economically significant given that this represents a major regulatory change affecting bank business models.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=deregulated states, control=still-regulated; shock=deregulation date
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Credit supply increases significantly after deregulation
